info.title: API.SH: Kaggle
info.description: The Kaggle API from API.SH: public Kaggle data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
A Kaggle competition's leaderboard: rank, score, team id and name, submission count, last submission date and team members (name, username, link, tier, avatar), plus the competition's metric and whether higher is better. `board=private` gives the final private leaderboard of a finished competition when the site publishes it. `total` is the number of teams. Pass `next_offset` back as `offset`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 2 credits per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/kaggle-competition-leaderboard

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Kaggle competitions: active or completed, by category (featured, research, getting started, playground, community, ...), with search, sort, prestige (medals or money) and participation filters. Each competition has its id, slug, title, short description, link, category, host and organization, reward, prize count, teams, competitors, submissions, start date, deadline, entry deadline, team size and daily submission limits, evaluation metric, license, forum id, tags and images, with the site's record in `raw`. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/kaggle-competitions

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order (default: the site's default; recently_closed for completed).

parameters.name: prestige
parameters.description: Only competitions awarding medals or money.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Search Kaggle's public datasets with every filter the site offers: sort, size, file type, license, tags and minimum usability, or list one user's or organization's datasets. Each dataset has its id, `ref` (owner/slug), title, subtitle, link, owner and creator, votes, views, downloads, notebook count, usability score, medal, license, size, file types, created and updated dates, images and tags, with the site's record in `raw`. `total` is the site's result count. 20 datasets a page; pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/kaggle-datasets

parameters.description: Order (default hottest, or relevance with q).

parameters.description: Only datasets of this Kaggle user or organization (username).

get.description:
One Kaggle notebook's metadata: id, ref, title, link, author, language, medal, votes, views, forks, version and version count, last update, the latest run (status, dates, run time, accelerator), the rendered output link, download-all link, data sources, output files (name, size, type, download link) and the comments link, with the site's records in `raw`. The notebook's code itself is not returned.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/kaggle-notebook

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Kaggle notebooks (code) by search, sort and language, or the notebooks of one competition, dataset, model or user. Each notebook has its id, ref (author/slug), title, link, author (name, username, tier, avatar), language, medal, votes, views, comments, line count, run time, version id, created, updated and last run dates, whether it has output files and its data sources, with the site's record in `raw`. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/kaggle-notebooks

apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
